slot.brief: Ask to rank given carbocations by stability, including one benzylic, one allylic, one vinyl-type case.

stem:
The correct stability order of the following carbocations is

I. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2^+$
II. $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2^+$
III. $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}^+$
IV. $\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^+$ (cyclopentadienyl cation)

verdicts.working: I is benzylic and strongly resonance-stabilized; II is allylic and resonance-stabilized. III lacks comparable resonance stabilization, while IV is a 4π antiaromatic cation and is least stable. Thus I > II > III > IV.
issues: The illustration labeled Option (B) appears to place the double bond adjacent to the cation, unlike the written allyl cation II.

working:
I – benzylic: resonance stabilized by phenyl ring (most stable).
II – allylic: resonance stabilized.
III – vinyl: no resonance, highly unstable.
IV – cyclopentadienyl cation: anti‑aromatic (4π e⁻), extremely unstable.
Stability: I > II > III > IV.

Independent check: I is benzylic and strongly resonance-stabilized; II is allylic and resonance-stabilized. III lacks comparable resonance stabilization, while IV is a 4π antiaromatic cation and is least stable. Thus I > II > III > IV.
solution:
Benzylic and allylic carbocations are resonance-stabilized; the benzylic ion has greater stabilization. The vinyl cation is highly unstable, while the cyclopentadienyl cation is antiaromatic with $4\pi$ electrons.
$$\text{I} > \text{II} > \text{III} > \text{IV}$$
